To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The dynamic range of the HB and HE electronics is 3.5 GeV, which is adequate to measure the expected QCD jets at the Lhc.

(i) the dynamic range of the HB and HE calorimeter electronics is large enough to accommodate the expected energy deposition of the LHC jets, (ii) the dynamic range is not a limiting factor for jet energy calibration, (iii) there are no concerns with the HB and HE electronics in the presence of the LHC beam halo, and (iv) the HB and HE readout electronics is expected to operate properly at the LHC luminosity
the maximum tower energy in the CMS HB/HE calorimeters will never exceed 3 TeV, and that the maximum tower in the CMS ECAL will never exceed 2.5 TeV.

the development of the CMS hadron calorimeter and the associated electronics, with a particular emphasis on the barrel section.
the study of the energy response and the dynamic range of the CMS barrel and endcap calorimeters.
the design of an efficient and robust system for the detection of the high energy particles produced in high energy collisions.
